Procurement buys the batch once, and the drawing, the electrical set and the price hold across every delivery. Package contractors who have fought inconsistent one-off cabins across a long alignment order it precisely to stop that variation for good, unit after unit after identical unit.","h3":"Uses","applications":["Metro and rail packages","Pipeline work fronts","Sequential deliveries","Batch-fabricated slim units"],"imageAlt":"Complete exterior of the prefabricated office cabin, 20 x 8 ft, module lines running vertically through the wall face along the 20 ft flank."},"20x10":{"h2":"20x10 ft, the standard multi-site office, by the batch","intro":"The reference office bought the procurement way: three, five or ten identical two-hundred-square-foot units on a single order, each matching the approved drawing to the millimetre. Site teams get a familiar office at every posting; head office gets one invoice, one specification and one warranty position across the fleet. This is the size most multi-site programmes standardise on, and the tier price at three units and again at higher counts is what separates this page from ordering one cabin three times.","h3":"Uses","applications":["Fleet standardisation","Single-order multi-site buys","Tiered batch pricing","Familiar office every posting"],"imageAlt":"The whole prefabricated office cabin, 20 x 10 ft, bolted panel modules meeting on a visible grid over the 20 ft length."},"20x12":{"h2":"20x12 ft, the wider standard for programme offices","intro":"Programmes that hold weekly reviews at every site standardise on the wider body, because the weekly meeting corner needs to exist at every location, not only at the flagship site. Ordered as a set, every location gets the same room in the same layout, so a visiting programme manager walks into a fully familiar office in every single city. The two extra feet cost the same modest step at every unit in the batch, and that consistency is worth more to a programme office than the extra floor area could ever be.","h3":"Uses","applications":["Programme review offices","Same room in every city","Batch-wide layouts","Visiting-manager familiarity"],"imageAlt":"Wide exterior view of the prefabricated office cabin, 20 x 12 ft, module lines running vertically through the wall face on the 12 ft end wall."},"30x10":{"h2":"30x10 ft, office plus store, repeated per site","intro":"The office-and-store split that most sites eventually improvise, fabricated identically for every location from the start: front section working, rear third partitioned and lockable. Instrument contractors and testing agencies who must secure equipment at each posting order it as their standard site unit. Because the partition sits on the same line in every unit, the security arrangement, the racking and even the key register work identically across the whole contract footprint, from the first posting to the last.","h3":"Uses","applications":["Per-site secure stores","Testing and instrument fleets","Identical security layouts","Contract-wide standards"],"imageAlt":"Overall view of the prefabricated office cabin, 30 x 10 ft, module lines running vertically through the wall face down the 30 ft side."},"40x8":{"h2":"40x8 ft, the linear unit for linear projects","intro":"Road, rail and transmission projects live along lines, and their offices follow: a forty-foot slim body repeated at each work front, fabricated in a batch and delivered as the alignment advances. The shape fits the leftover land that linear projects actually have, and batch fabrication holds the specification steady across every chainage. Contractors order the set at award and schedule deliveries against mobilisation, so each new front opens with its office already committed, priced and on the schedule.","h3":"Uses","applications":["Alignment work fronts","Road and rail mobilisation","Transmission line packages","Chainage-by-chainage delivery"],"imageAlt":"Long exterior view of the prefabricated office cabin, 40 x 8 ft, bolted panel modules meeting on a visible grid along the full 40 ft run."},"40x10":{"h2":"40x10 ft, the package headquarters, one per package","intro":"Large programmes split into packages, and each package office is this: four hundred square feet of departmentalised floor, identical at every package so reporting, filing and even furniture orders repeat cleanly. Buying them as a set at award locks the price for later packages and removes the specification drift that creeps in when each package buys its own. Programme directors who have consolidated five mismatched offices into one standard remember exactly why this page exists and order accordingly at the next award.","h3":"Uses","applications":["One office per package","Award-stage set purchases","No specification drift","Departmentalised standards"],"imageAlt":"Side-on view of the prefabricated office cabin, 40 x 10 ft, module lines running vertically through the wall face across the 40 ft elevation."},"20x20":{"h2":"20x20 ft, the square training unit, deployed in sets","intro":"Induction has to happen at every site of a large contract, and the square floor is the induction room: open, central, seating in rows or clusters. Ordered as a set, every location trains in the same room with the same layout, which safety teams value because the induction itself becomes standard. The two-piece build travels like the smaller units, so even the remotest sites of the contract are not excluded from it. One drawing approval covers the entire training estate for the full life of the programme.","h3":"Uses","applications":["Site induction rooms","Safety training estates","Set-deployed squares","Standardised inductions"],"imageAlt":"Full-length view of the prefabricated office cabin, 20 x 20 ft, bolted panel modules meeting on a visible grid around the 20 ft square plan."},"40x12":{"h2":"40x12 ft, the flagship unit of a standardised fleet","intro":"The largest unit in a standardised order: the regional or lead-site office that anchors a fleet of smaller identical cabins. Fabricated on the same batch drawing discipline, it shares its surfaces, its openings and its electrical logic with every junior unit in the order, so the fleet reads as one estate rather than a collection. Contractors running a hub-and-spoke site structure order one of these with each cluster of smaller units, and the tier pricing counts the whole mixed order as one quantity for the discount.","h3":"Uses","applications":["Lead-site anchors","Hub-and-spoke fleets","Mixed-size single orders","Estate-consistent flagships"],"imageAlt":"Full elevation of the prefabricated office cabin, 40 x 12 ft, bolted panel modules meeting on a visible grid over the 40 by 12 ft body."}},"portable-office-container":{"h2":"Portable Office Container sizes built for relocation","guidanceLine":"Every unit carries reinforced lifting points and protected services as standard.","10x10":{"h2":"10x10 ft, the unit that moves with the work","intro":"A gate office that follows the project: reinforced corner lifting points, services routed in protected conduit, and a frame stiffened for repeated craning. Event operators and short-phase contractors shift this compact unit several times in a season, and the hardening is what lets them do it without a repair bill after every move. Where an ordinary cabin is placed once and left, this one is designed around the assumption that the truck is coming back for it, this season and the next and the one after.","h3":"Uses","applications":["Event circuit offices","Short-phase works","Season-by-season moves","Repeated crane handling"],"imageAlt":"Portable office container, 10 x 10 ft, pale blue upper panel over a dark grey base, two windows and a central door seen from the corner."},"20x8":{"h2":"20x8 ft, the slim mover for tight repeated drops","intro":"The narrow body that goes where the next placement is tighter than the last: reinforced for lifting, slim enough for urban lanes, services sealed against the knocks of transit. Utility contractors moving crews between road openings keep one permanently on the truck rotation, dropping it fresh at each new stretch of road. The protected wiring loom means the office is live within an hour of touching down, and just as quickly disconnected when the stretch is done, the crew moves on and the next opening is already waiting.","h3":"Uses","applications":["Utility crew rotations","Urban road openings","Hour-to-live placements","Truck-rotation offices"],"imageAlt":"Complete exterior of the portable office container, 20 x 8 ft, a strengthened base frame sized for repeated craning along the 20 ft flank."},"20x10":{"h2":"20x10 ft, the standard office, hardened to travel","intro":"The familiar two-hundred-square-foot office rebuilt around movement: lifting interfaces engineered to the unit\'s completed weight, glazing protected for transit, services terminating in a single armoured connection point. Contractors whose projects run in phases across a region relocate it between sites instead of buying twice. Each move costs transport and a crane, not refurbishment, which changes the arithmetic of owning one office across many postings entirely, which is the calculation this whole line is built on.","h3":"Uses","applications":["Phase-to-phase relocation","Regional project rotations","One office, many postings","Transit-protected standard"],"imageAlt":"Portable office container, 20 x 10 ft, white upper panel over a charcoal base with four windows along the twenty foot flank."},"20x12":{"h2":"20x12 ft, moving width without moving damage","intro":"The wider floor with the meeting corner, built to survive the journey between placements: stiffened top frame, protected service runs, lifting points matched to the extra width. Project teams that host client reviews and then move on take it because the meeting room travels along with the project instead of being rebuilt from nothing each phase. What normally suffers in a relocated cabin is the fit-out, and here the fit-out is anchored and shielded from the outset, specifically because relocation is the plan.","h3":"Uses","applications":["Travelling review rooms","Client-facing phase offices","Protected fit-outs","Width that relocates"],"imageAlt":"Wide exterior view of the portable office container, 20 x 12 ft, a strengthened base frame sized for repeated craning on the 12 ft end wall."},"30x10":{"h2":"30x10 ft, office and store that redeploy together","intro":"The partitioned office-plus-store as a single relocatable body: instruments stay in their lockable rear room during the move, and the whole unit lifts as one sealed piece. Survey and geotechnical teams working campaign-style across sites redeploy it with the equipment still racked and locked inside, saving a full pack-up and set-down at every single move. The stiffened frame is what makes travelling loaded acceptable, and that capability is the whole difference between this and simply partitioning an ordinary cabin.","h3":"Uses","applications":["Campaign survey teams","Loaded relocations","Instrument rooms in transit","Redeployable stores"],"imageAlt":"Overall view of the portable office container, 30 x 10 ft, a strengthened base frame sized for repeated craning down the 30 ft side."},"40x8":{"h2":"40x8 ft, the long unit that follows the alignment","intro":"Linear projects advance, and this office advances with them: a forty-foot slim body lifted from chainage to chainage as fronts complete. The length demands proper lifting engineering, and that is precisely what the hardened frame and matched lift points provide. Road and pipeline contractors move it three or four times across a package instead of placing a new cabin at each front, and the protected loom re-terminates at each drop without an electrician rebuilding the connection from scratch at every single drop.","h3":"Uses","applications":["Advancing work fronts","Chainage relocations","Three moves per package","Re-terminating services"],"imageAlt":"Long exterior view of the portable office container, 40 x 8 ft, reinforced lifting points built into each corner along the full 40 ft run."},"40x10":{"h2":"40x10 ft, headquarters that transfer between projects","intro":"A full four-hundred-square-foot project office engineered to serve consecutive projects rather than one: transferred by crane and trailer at each demobilisation, arriving at the next award with its zones, services and fittings intact. Contractors treat it as plant, moving it project to project on the asset register, and the hardening is what preserves its value across those transfers. The alternative is buying a headquarters at every award and abandoning that embedded value at every project close-out.","h3":"Uses","applications":["Project-to-project transfer","Demobilisation moves","Offices held as plant","Value across awards"],"imageAlt":"Side-on view of the portable office container, 40 x 10 ft, a strengthened base frame sized for repeated craning across the 40 ft elevation."},"20x20":{"h2":"20x20 ft, the square that splits, moves and rejoins","intro":"The two-piece square with relocation designed into the joint: each half lifts separately on its own reinforced points, travels as a standard load, and rejoins with the sealed floor strip and paired electrical sets re-mating at the new site. Training rooms and control rooms that must exist at each phase of a long programme move this way. Rejoining is a procedure, not an improvisation, because the joint was engineered for its fifth mating, and not merely its first, which is where improvised joints fail.","h3":"Uses","applications":["Two-lift relocations","Re-mating joints","Phase-following control rooms","Programme training squares"],"imageAlt":"Full-length view of the portable office container, 20 x 20 ft, reinforced lifting points built into each corner around the 20 ft square plan."},"40x12":{"h2":"40x12 ft, the largest office we build to move","intro":"Four hundred and eighty square feet engineered for a life of placements: the heaviest unit in this line, and therefore the one where lifting-point engineering and frame stiffening matter most. Organisations running long rotations, mine services, large EPC houses, plant hire, keep one or two circulating between commitments. It is the most office that can follow the work as a single body, and the hardening premium is what keeps it working after the fifth site instead of giving up somewhere around the second.","h3":"Uses","applications":["Long asset rotations","Mine and EPC services","Circulating head offices","Fifth-site durability"],"imageAlt":"Full elevation of the portable office container, 40 x 12 ft, reinforced lifting points built into each corner over the 40 by 12 ft body."}},"small-office-cabin":{"h2":"Small Office Cabin sizes for one to four people","guidanceLine":"Three compact sizes only. Larger floors live on our main office range page.","10x10":{"h2":"10x10 ft, the two-person office in its element","intro":"One hundred square feet arranged for two people who share a task: a security supervisor beside the CCTV desk, a cashier with the records, a doctor with an assistant. This page\'s whole purpose is the compact brief, so the smallest size is its centre of gravity rather than its afterthought. The cabin lands, connects and works the same day, and the nine-foot ceiling keeps a small footprint from feeling like a box. Most buyers here never needed anything larger, and nothing larger is ever pushed at them here.","h3":"Uses","applications":["Two-person duty rooms","CCTV and security desks","Cash and records points","Clinic side rooms"],"imageAlt":"Full side view of the small office cabin, 10 x 10 ft, a single-bay body with one door and one window across the 10 ft wall."},"20x8":{"h2":"20x8 ft, three desks where depth does not exist","intro":"The compact answer for narrow ground: three desks in a row against the long wall, a door at the end, and a footprint that slots beside a gate, along a boundary or behind a showroom. Small teams that outgrew a guard-post-sized room but have no depth to spare step up to this shape and stop there. It shares the slim body of the bigger ranges but is bought here for a different reason: not because the plot is a corridor, but because the team is three people and perfectly honest with itself about staying that way.","h3":"Uses","applications":["Three-desk slim offices","Beside-the-gate teams","Behind-showroom rooms","Small teams, narrow ground"],"imageAlt":"Complete exterior of the small office cabin, 20 x 8 ft, a compact body proportioned for a tight site corner along the 20 ft flank."},"20x10":{"h2":"20x10 ft, the largest office this page will sell you","intro":"Two hundred square feet for four people, and deliberately the ceiling of this range: anything bigger belongs on the main range page with the full nine-size ladder. Kept here because a four-person office is still a small office, and the buyer comparing it with the two smaller sizes is making a compact-office decision, not a site-headquarters decision dressed up small. The fit-out matches the smaller sizes exactly, so growing from the 10x10 to this floor changes the floor area and changes nothing else at all.","h3":"Uses","applications":["Four-person offices","Compact-office ceiling","Growth from two to four","Same fit-out, more floor"],"imageAlt":"The whole small office cabin, 20 x 10 ft, a single-bay body with one door and one window over the 20 ft length."}},"labor-colony":{"h2":"Every labour colony size, and the site each one runs","60x24-gplus1":{"h2":"60x24 ft G+1, 2880 sq ft planned for 58 to 72 workers","intro":"The smallest colony dormitory holds 58 to 72 workers over two floors and usually anchors a compact site with one toilet block beside it. At 2,880 square feet it fits plots where a longer building will not, and the flat colony rate of Rs 675 per square foot keeps its cost at Rs 19,44,000 ex-GST. Phased sites place it first and let later blocks join the planned services spine. Ask for the colony starter plan and the quotation includes the matching toilet block position on your plot. Site lighting on the access side is part of the standard scope.","h3":"Use-cases","applications":["Crews of 58 plus","Phase-one site setup","Occupancy-normed planning","48-hour fixed quotation"],"imageAlt":"Labour colony, 60x24 ft G+1, from the front left with the end stair, two floors on a 60 ft footprint in the multi-block housing build."},"90x24-gplus1":{"h2":"90x24 ft G+1, 4320 sq ft planned for 86 to 108 workers","intro":"Ninety feet of building over two floors sleeps 86 to 108 workers, which matches the crew of a mid-size civil package. This is the configuration our own costing sheet uses as its reference for the whole cluster, so quotations on it turn around fastest. The dormitory pairs with a four-seat toilet block on the standard site plan, and the 4,320 square feet price out at Rs 29,16,000 ex-GST with nothing added for size. Because it is the costing reference, its drawings are the most exercised in the library and surprises are rare. Its toilet-block pairing is drawn at four stalls per floor.","h3":"Use-cases","applications":["Crews of 86 plus","Phase-one site setup","Occupancy-normed planning","48-hour fixed quotation"],"imageAlt":"Labour colony, 90x24 ft G+1, from the left corner at the stair end, two floors on a 90 ft footprint in the multi-block housing build."},"90x24-gplus2":{"h2":"90x24 ft G+2, 6480 sq ft planned for 129 to 162 workers","intro":"Adding a third floor to the 90 ft footprint lifts capacity to 129 to 162 workers without taking one extra foot of plot, which is why tight urban sites choose it. Stair towers at the building end serve all three levels, and the structure is engineered for the extra storey from the base up rather than adapted later. The 6,480 square feet list at Rs 43,74,000 ex-GST at the same flat rate every other size uses. Local height clearances are the one item to confirm early, and our drawing pack includes what approvers ask for.","h3":"Use-cases","applications":["Crews of 129 plus","Phase-one site setup","Occupancy-normed planning","48-hour fixed quotation"],"imageAlt":"Labour colony, 90x24 ft G+2, from the stair end on the left, three floors on a 90 ft footprint in the multi-block housing build."},"120x24-gplus1":{"h2":"120x24 ft G+1, 5760 sq ft planned for 115 to 144 workers","intro":"The 120 ft two-floor building is the workhorse of large colonies: 115 to 144 workers in one block, long straight rooms that furnish quickly, and a footprint that packs efficiently in rows with fire separation between them. Most multi-building colonies are laid out as repeats of this unit. Its 5,760 square feet total Rs 38,88,000 ex-GST, the figure the hub record carries. Row spacing and fire separation dimensions for repeat layouts ship with the first quotation as standard. Gate distance and muster areas are marked on the same layout sheet.","h3":"Use-cases","applications":["Crews of 115 plus","Phase-one site setup","Occupancy-normed planning","48-hour fixed quotation"],"imageAlt":"Labour colony, 120x24 ft G+1, from the front left with the end stair, two floors on a 120 ft footprint in the multi-block housing build."},"118x30-gplus1":{"h2":"118x30 ft G+1, 7080 sq ft planned for 142 to 177 workers","intro":"The 30 ft wide body changes the internal planning: deeper rooms, wider aisles and space for in-block amenities that the 24 ft buildings push to separate blocks. With 142 to 177 workers over two floors and 7,080 square feet, it suits employers who want fewer, better buildings rather than more repeats. Cost follows the same rule as every size, Rs 47,79,000 ex-GST. Employers housing supervisors alongside crews usually reserve the wide body\'s deeper rooms for that purpose. Verandah options along the long face are quoted on request.","h3":"Use-cases","applications":["Crews of 142 plus","Phase-one site setup","Occupancy-normed planning","48-hour fixed quotation"],"imageAlt":"Labour colony, 118x30 ft G+1, from the left corner at the stair end, two floors on the wide 30 ft body in the multi-block housing build."},"120x24-gplus2":{"h2":"120x24 ft G+2, 8640 sq ft planned for 173 to 216 workers","intro":"Three floors on the 120 ft footprint make the largest single dormitory we build: 173 to 216 workers, 8,640 square feet, one stair core serving all levels. A pair of these houses a four-hundred-strong workforce on remarkably little land. It prices at Rs 58,32,000 ex-GST, and like every configuration on this page that figure is area times the flat colony rate, nothing else. Where two of these stand together the services spine between them is designed once and shared by both. Water storage for all floors sits on the stair-core roof slab.","h3":"Use-cases","applications":["Crews of 173 plus","Phase-one site setup","Occupancy-normed planning","48-hour fixed quotation"],"imageAlt":"Labour colony, 120x24 ft G+2, from the stair end on the left, three floors on a 120 ft footprint in the multi-block housing build."}},"labor-sheds":{"20x10":{"h2":"20x10 ft Labour Shed: 200 sq ft With a Single Bunk Row","intro":"The smallest published shed. At 10 ft wide there is room for one bunk row along a single long wall and a clear walking aisle beside it, so the plan stays simple and the exit is never blocked by a bed. It suits a small gang, a night shift crew or a remote outpost where a full hall is not justified. Below this footprint a shed stops making sense: the frame, roof and door cost much the same whatever the length, so an insulated PUF porta cabin becomes the better buy.","h3":"","applications":[],"imageAlt":"20x10 ft labour shed in ivory white cladding, front-left view, with a continuous louvre band under the eaves"},"20x15":{"h2":"20x15 ft Labour Shed: 300 sq ft, Two Rows and Aisle","intro":"Fifteen feet of width is the point where a second bunk row becomes practical. Bunks sit against both long walls with a central aisle between them, which roughly doubles the beds without doubling the roof or the slab. This is the first size that behaves like a proper dormitory rather than a bunk room, and it is a common choice for a single trade gang working one defined package on a short site programme.","h3":"","applications":[],"imageAlt":"20x15 ft labour shed in olive-green cladding, front-left view, with two doors along the long wall"},"20x20":{"h2":"20x20 ft Labour Shed: 400 sq ft With a Wider Centre Aisle","intro":"At 20 ft square the hall becomes genuinely comfortable to move through. The extra width goes into the central aisle and into locker space at each end, so men can dress and store kit without standing on each other at shift change. Cleaning is faster too, because the aisle takes a trolley rather than forcing hand work between beds. Choose this when occupancy is steady and the shed will stand for several months.","h3":"","applications":[],"imageAlt":"20x20 ft labour shed in blue-grey cladding, front-left view, two doors spaced along the long wall"},"20x25":{"h2":"20x25 ft Labour Shed: 500 sq ft, Mid-Point Second Exit","intro":"Length is what changes here rather than width. At 25 ft the walk from the far bunk to a single door gets long, so a second personnel door goes into the long wall near the mid-point. Two exits shorten travel distance in an emergency and give the hall a second cross-flow air path on still days. This is the size at which exit planning starts to drive the hall layout rather than simply follow it.","h3":"","applications":[],"imageAlt":"20x25 ft labour shed in champagne cladding with a double-leaf door and canopy on the gable end"},"20x30":{"h2":"20x30 ft Labour Shed: 600 sq ft With a Door at Each End","intro":"Thirty feet gives a full-length central aisle running door to door, which is the cleanest circulation this product achieves. Air enters through the louvre band along both walls, crosses the bunks and leaves at the ridge without anything blocking the path. It is the size we use as the reference plan on the technical drawing, because at 30 ft every control the shed depends on is visible in a single view.","h3":"","applications":[],"imageAlt":"20x30 ft labour shed in pearl-grey cladding, front-left view, with a ridge ventilator along the apex"},"20x40":{"h2":"20x40 ft Labour Shed: 800 sq ft, Three Distributed Exits","intro":"The largest published shed and the lowest rate per square foot, because one roof and one slab now cover twice the floor of the 20x20. Two long bunk rows face a full-length aisle, with three doors distributed along the length so no bunk sits far from an exit. Beyond this footprint the frame needs a wider clear span, so the shed is engineered and quoted individually rather than taken from the published six.","h3":"","applications":[],"imageAlt":"20x40 ft labour shed in graphite cladding, front-left view, with a continuous eaves louvre band"}},"labor-hutments":{"h2":"Every labour hutment size, and the rooms each block gives","60x24-gplus1":{"h2":"60x24 ft G+1, 2880 sq ft planned for 58 to 72 workers","intro":"The small hutment gives two floors of individual rooms for 58 to 72 workers, each room with its own door, window, fan and board. Short passages serve a handful of rooms per floor, so gangs keep to their own space and belongings stay behind a lock. It is the configuration for smaller mixed crews, and its 2,880 square feet come in at Rs 19,82,880 ex-GST. Couples employed together on site are usually allocated the end rooms, which sit apart from the gang rooms. Every room lock is master-keyed for the site office.","h3":"Use-cases","applications":["Crews of 58 plus","Phase-one site setup","Occupancy-normed planning","48-hour fixed quotation"],"imageAlt":"Labour hutment, 60x24 ft G+1, from the front left with the end stair, two floors on a 60 ft footprint in the room-block hutment build."},"90x24-gplus1":{"h2":"90x24 ft G+1, 4320 sq ft planned for 86 to 108 workers","intro":"Ninety feet of rooms over two floors houses 86 to 108 workers in the best-balanced room block we make.
